title: Ada and the Thorn
premise: Marguerite Amberdale, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies — and every entry after it ends in a country that no longer exists. Hunted by the Inquisitors who exiled him and shadowed by Ada, a thorn-marked girl who claims to remember a future she never lived, Marguerite must retrace his own erased past to find the Door of Unmaking, the only way out of Vhalen before the prophecy closes. Along the way he learns the guild itself wrote the prophecy, trading his exile for its own survival. In the end, Marguerite chooses truth over loyalty: he burns the ledgers, opens the Door at the cost of his storm-gift, and leaves Ada behind in a country reborn from its own ashes.
about_author: X. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated books in a coastal city that has since changed its name twice. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things everyone else agrees to forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. In the guild's candlelit counting-house, Marguerite balances impossible accounts — bottled thunder, borrowed years — when he finds tonight's date already written in a prophecy book a century old, in handwriting unnervingly like his own. The beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Girl with Thorns in Her Hair
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Ada arrives at the guild claiming to remember events from tomorrow, her arms scarred with living thorns that bloom when she lies. The guildmaster accepts her as cargo rather than guest. The beat: wary fascination; Marguerite recognizes his own exile in her strangeness.

chapters.title: What the Guild Trades
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Guided through the vaults, Ada sees the guild's true inventory: memories, borders, one unlabeled door. She lies to protect Marguerite and her thorns bleed. The beat: first loyalty, first cost — she decides he is worth bleeding for.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Summons
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. An Inquisitor named Corvane arrives with a warrant written in the same hand as the prophecy, demanding the ledger of dates. Marguerite hides the book inside a memory he sold years ago and cannot retrieve. The beat: panic sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada's thorn-memories reveal Vhalen was erased from maps and minds alike — and that Marguerite's storm-calling caused it. She confronts him; he remembers nothing. The beat: betrayal, and the terrible tenderness of telling someone their own crime.

chapters.title: Storm Without Weather
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Pressed by Ada's accusations, Marguerite reaches for his gift and finds it caged by his exile-oath. He breaks a small law instead — reading the sealed guildmaster's ledger — and learns the guild co-authored the prophecy. The beat: disillusionment hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Rain
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The prophecy grants nine days before Vhalen finishes unexisting. Rain falls upward in the market; citizens forget mid-sentence. Ada and Marguerite steal the guild's map of erased places. The beat: urgency binding them into partners.

chapters.title: Corvane's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Cornered by Corvane, Marguerite expects arrest but receives an offer: testify against the guild and regain his name. Corvane reveals he too appears in the prophecy — on its final page. The beat: temptation, and the discovery that even hunters are trapped.

chapters.title: The Memory Broker
chapters.summary: POV Ada. To recover Marguerite's hidden memories, they seek Sef, a broker who deals in recollection. The price: one of Ada's thorn-memories of the future. She pays without telling him. The beat: sacrifice made in silence, loyalty outpacing honesty.

chapters.title: What I Did to Vhalen
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Restored memories flood back: Marguerite called the storm to save rebels, and the crown answered by erasing the whole country — with the guild holding the pen. His grief turns to fury at his own naivety. The beat: reckoning with guilt.

chapters.title: Halfway House of Forgotten Roads
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Sheltering in an inn that exists on no road, they meet others half-erased — a ferryman, twin sisters sharing one name. Ada realizes her thorns grow from the same erasure; she is Vhalen's memory given flesh. The beat: identity crisis transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Returning to confront the guildmaster, Marguerite finds her dying, her body unraveling like ink in water. She confesses: the Door of Unmaking opens only for someone the country still remembers — and begs him to burn nothing until he understands. The beat: ambiguous deathbed wisdom.

chapters.title: Ledger Fire
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Interpreting 'understand' differently, Marguerite burns the trade-ledgers to free the guild's stored memories back into the world. Ada watches him choose truth over the institution that sheltered him — and fears what freedom will cost. The beat: awe shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Page
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Corvane captures them, but the freed memories reach him too: he was Vhalen's chief judge, complicit in the erasure, his page in the prophecy a sentence he wrote himself. He lets them go and walks into the dissolving streets. The beat: justice outside the law, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Three Days Left
chapters.summary: POV Ada. With three days remaining, Ada admits what she paid Sef: her memory of how the story ends. She knows the Door demands a life and has decided whose. Marguerite refuses to let her decide alone. The beat: love declared through argument.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Following roads that surface only when walked by someone Vhalen remembers, they cross a landscape stitching itself back together — orchards blooming from rumor, bells ringing names. Marguerite feels the country forgiving him. The beat: grief transmuted into belonging.

chapters.title: Sef's Price Refunded
chapters.summary: POV Ada. They ambush Sef to reclaim Ada's sold future-memory, but Sef has already read it and warns them both endings are worse than they fear. Ada takes the memory back anyway. The beat: courage as choosing knowledge over comfort.

chapters.title: The Door of Unmaking
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. At the heart of old Vhalen stands the Door, guarded by the country's collective memory wearing many faces. It names its price: a storm-caller's gift, freely surrendered, to unmake the erasure from within. The beat: the trap revealed — the sacrifice is his, not Ada's.

chapters.title: Ada's Argument
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada tries to trick the Door with her thorn-self, offering herself as Vhalen's memory returned. The Door refuses: memory cannot pay for memory. Marguerite steps forward before she can fight it. The beat: the pain of being saved from self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Storm Surrendered
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Climax. Marguerite pours his storm-gift into the Door, reliving the original tempest as it reverses — Vhalen remaking itself street by street while he empties into weatherless calm. He speaks the truth of his crime aloud so the country hears it. The beat: catharsis, loss, absolution.

chapters.title: A Country Reborn
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Vhalen returns to maps and minds; Ada's thorns fall away, leaving ordinary scars. But the Door took more than the storm — Marguerite's name among the remembered. He can stay invisible forever or walk out of the country that no longer needs him. The beat: bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: Ada and the Thorn
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite, closing with Ada. Marguerite chooses exile again — freely this time — and Ada chooses to forget her future and share his unwritten one. They leave through the guild's plain front door into rain that falls the right way. Final beat: loyalty and truth reconciled at last.
